Custom Wood Stair Treads in Tampa Bay: A Homeowner's Guide

How to choose custom wood stair treads in Tampa Bay: solid vs overlay vs floating treads, White Oak vs Ash, Florida humidity, measuring, code limits, and what affects price.

Updated 2026-10-22

Key takeaways

  • Custom stair treads are cut to your staircase's real measurements instead of a stock size, so they sit flush without on-site trimming.
  • Overlay treads cover existing treads (for example after removing carpet); solid treads replace them; floating treads are thick blocks for open staircases.
  • White Oak and Ash are both hard, durable species. White Oak is the more popular choice for matching modern Florida floors; Ash is lighter in color with a bolder grain.
  • In Florida's humidity, treads should be sealed on every side and acclimated indoors before installation to resist cupping.
  • Price depends on species, thickness, depth, length, nosing profile, finish, and the number of treads and risers.

Types of stair treads

The right tread depends on what is under it today and how the staircase is built. PalmCraft makes four tread types and matching risers.

  • Solid treads: Full-thickness hardwood treads that replace the existing treads. The standard choice for new construction and full stair renovations.
  • Overlay (retrofit) treads: Thinner treads installed over existing treads, usually after carpet is removed. They avoid tearing out the stair structure, which keeps the project faster and less disruptive.
  • Bullnose treads: Treads with a rounded front edge (nosing). The profile softens the look of the stair and is common in traditional and transitional homes.
  • Floating treads: Thick block treads for open, cantilevered staircases where the ends and underside are visible, so every face has to be finished.
  • Risers: The vertical boards between treads. Matching or painted risers complete the staircase and hide the old structure.

White Oak vs Ash: which wood to choose

PalmCraft makes stair treads in White Oak and Ash. Both are hard, dense hardwoods that stand up to daily foot traffic.

White Oak has a tight, straight grain and a warm tone. It takes stain consistently, which makes it the easier species to match to existing oak or engineered floors, and it is the most requested option for modern and coastal Florida interiors.

Ash is lighter, with a bolder, more open grain. It suits natural, Scandinavian, and light contemporary interiors, and it pairs well with light floors when finished clear.

If you are matching an existing floor, start from the floor: bring a sample or a clear photo, and approve a finished sample on the tread species before the full order is finished.

Why Florida humidity matters for stair treads

Wood absorbs and releases moisture as indoor humidity changes. In Tampa Bay's climate, a tread that is finished only on the top face can take on moisture through its underside and ends, which is a common cause of cupping and gaps.

Two habits prevent most problems: seal the tread on all sides, and let the treads acclimate inside the conditioned house for several days before installation. Keep the air conditioning running during and after the install so the wood settles at the same moisture level as the rest of the home.

How to measure your stairs

Measure every step separately — older staircases are rarely identical from top to bottom. For each step, record the width (wall to wall or wall to open end), the depth (back of the step to the front edge), and the height of the riser below it.

Note whether each side ends at a wall or is open; open ends need a return (a finished end) on the tread. If you are installing overlay treads, measure over the existing treads after the carpet and tack strips are removed.

Florida's residential building code sets limits that new or rebuilt stairs must meet: a maximum riser height of 7¾ inches and a minimum tread depth of 10 inches, with a nosing of ¾ to 1¼ inches on stairs that have solid risers and treads shallower than 11 inches. Check with your local building department for your project.

If you are unsure, PalmCraft can measure the staircase during a consultation.

What affects the price of custom stair treads

Stair treads are priced per tread and per riser, so the total depends on the staircase and the choices below. You get an itemized quote before anything is produced.

  • Species: White Oak or Ash.
  • Thickness: Overlay, standard solid, or thick floating block.
  • Size: Depth and length of each tread.
  • Profile: Square, bullnose, or returned ends on open sides.
  • Finish: Unfinished, clear-sealed, or stained to match your floor.
  • Quantity: Number of treads, risers, and any landing pieces.

Replacing carpeted stairs with wood

Replacing carpet with wood is one of the most common stair projects in Tampa Bay homes. After the carpet, pad, and tack strips come off, the existing treads are usually construction-grade lumber that was never meant to be seen.

Overlay treads are typically the quickest route: they install over the existing structure, and new risers cover the old ones. If the existing treads are damaged or the nosing is in the wrong place, full solid treads are the better fix.

Frequently asked questions

Does PalmCraft make custom stair treads?

Yes. PalmCraft Cabinets makes custom wood stair treads and risers to measure for homes in Tampa Bay, in White Oak and Ash, as solid, overlay, bullnose, or floating treads.

What is the difference between overlay and solid stair treads?

Overlay treads are installed over the existing treads, usually after carpet removal, without tearing out the stair structure. Solid treads replace the existing treads entirely and suit new construction or stairs with damaged treads.

Is White Oak or Ash better for stair treads?

Both are hard, durable hardwoods suitable for stairs. White Oak has a tighter grain and takes stain consistently, so it is easier to match to existing floors. Ash is lighter with a bolder grain and suits natural, light interiors.

Can stair treads be stained to match my existing floor?

Yes. Bring a floor sample or a clear photo, and approve a finished sample on the tread species before the full order is finished. Matching from a sample is far more reliable than matching from a color name.

How do I keep wood stair treads from cupping in Florida?

Seal the treads on all sides, let them acclimate inside the air-conditioned home for several days before installation, and keep the air conditioning running so indoor humidity stays stable.

What are the code requirements for stairs in Florida?

Florida's residential building code limits riser height to 7¾ inches and requires a minimum tread depth of 10 inches, with a ¾ to 1¼ inch nosing on stairs with solid risers where the tread is shallower than 11 inches. Confirm requirements with your local building department.

How much do custom stair treads cost?

Price depends on species, thickness, tread size, profile, finish, and the number of treads and risers. PalmCraft provides an itemized quote after reviewing your measurements or measuring the staircase.
